svg.text: What each stage reads: a sample to discover, everything in batches to evaluate, the cases' own history to infer.
propose from the data's shape; build
for the screen ids, in batches
propose · from what the data looks like
→ an idea and its code: link(), an
aggregate, build() - no data joined yet
build · in batches, for the screen ids
build() a chunk at a time → one column
for the screen ids - the same steps as at
a cache only: if the screen customers hold
under half a source, their rows are reused
screen · as with the original data
base vs base + feature → verified or not
the full splits and test (OOT) are never
the full splits and the whole source,
4M rows at a time, only the columns
b · joined rows to disk, by id chunk
each batch's rows go to their chunk;
the ids × events table is never in memory
disk: about the linkage's "GB at full size"
by day / week / month: split by key
into ~1 GB parts, one part at a time
d · build per chunk, then the model
build() on 50k ids at a time → one
column for every id of the splits
XGBoost retrained on full train / valid
read in batches all the same
c · score base vs base + new
🎯 target cases go straight to inference

g.text: Sizes and memory figures are illustrative; batch, chunk and part sizes are the defaults.
